name: National Registration Identity Card Number (NRIC Number)
issuer: the Malaysian Government's national registration (the sheet doesn't name the office)
note: Malaysia's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: (updated March 2023) the Inland Revenue Board's TIN goes to every Malaysian citizen aged 18 and over, but its length varies (IG and nine to eleven digits), so the number kept here is its stated functional equivalent: the National Registration Identity Card Number, a unique 12-digit number issued to Malaysian citizens and permanent residents and used by the Board to identify taxpayers. The sheet doesn't name the office that issues the NRIC (the National Registration Department). Read as given on registration, to citizens and residents. No check rule, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Malaysia: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: TIN will be issued to all Malaysian citizens who attained the age of 18 years old and above. ... the Malaysian National Registration Identity Card Number (NRIC Number). The NRIC Number is a unique 12-digit number issued to Malaysian citizens and permanent residents and is used by the IRBM to identify its taxpayers.
